newsitem.title: USA: DuPont Q1 selling prices hurt by strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: DuPont Q1 selling prices hurt by strong dlr.

text.p: DuPont Co said Wednesday that volumes in most of its chemicals and specialties markets were strong in the first quarter but selling prices were hurt by the strong dollar.
The company said increased revenues from petroleum principally reflected higher oil and natural gas prices.
First quarter sales of chemicals and specialties were up three percent to $5.9 billion, while petroleum sales were up 15 percent to $5.4 billion.
Chemicals and specialties volumes were up seven percent: in the United States six percent, in Europe five percent, and in other regions combined 13 percent.

Selling prices in those two segments declined four percent overall. Selling prices were down one percent for the United States and an average of seven percent for other regions, with five percentage points of the decline due to currency, it said.
Overall sales for the first quarter were $11.2 billion, up four percent from a year earlier.

"Our results this quarter reflect record petroleum and near-record fibers segment earnings, up 55 percent and 30 percent, respectively, from last year's first quarter," DuPont President and Chief Executive John Krol said in a statement.
